doc.title: Rick Margitza interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 22, 2024

title: Deciding to move to Paris
summary: After a decade in New York and Europe festival work, joining the Moutin Reunion Quartet and an offered apartment prompted the move to Paris.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: What prompted you to relocate to Paris?

Well I was living in New York — well so I lived, at this point I was in New Orleans and then when the Blue Note thing happened and Miles happened it was 1989 or so, and I always wanted to move to New York. So I moved to New York around ’89 and was there for about ten years. And at that point you know in New York there still is not — you know you’re doing these little gigs but you’re not making a lot of money and since I was kind of new on the scene I got calls to come over to Europe to do jazz festivals, and that’s where the majority of American jazz musicians make decent money is by coming over to Europe and playing you know, unless you’re really famous and you’re able to tour around the country with your own band, but that takes a while to happen. So it really didn’t happen for me. I was coming over to Europe and making more of a name for myself that way. And I always loved Paris. And I thought this would be a cool place to live because just the city itself, and I realized it’s kind of the hub of Europe so it makes getting to Germany, to Austria, to Belgium, to Amsterdam, to London on a train really easy. So of course because what we do there is a lot of traveling involved, but the trains are always much cooler than the airports. So I kind of planted that seed and I had some friends who were living in Paris, but I never really did anything proactive about finding my way over here, just kind of thinking it would be a cool thing to do. And it was in 2000 — well before that I mean — I think around 2001 I got asked to join a French band call the Moutin Reunion Quartet. It’s twin brothers, and the bass player, Francois, lived in New York. His brother Louis lives in Paris, and I became friends with Francois. And they had a working band and their saxophone player left. So Francois asked me if I wanted to join the band. So that means I was coming over to France even more. I was living in an illegal sublet on the upper West Side and we got caught so I was going to have to find another place to live in New York, which is always very traumatic and not cheap. And a relationship I was in with a girl had ended like a couple of months before that, and so there was three things. And then a friend of mine in Paris who knew I was talking about moving here, he actually called me and said, “Rick, I’m leaving, if you want you could have my apartment.”

Yeah. So the universe gave me like four major signs, and I said if I don’t do this something bad is going to happen. And I said, and if I don’t do it I also am going to regret not taking the chance. So yeah, and I said if I didn’t like it I could always move back.
